body: The Strength and Armour Piercing characteristics of any impact hits caused by an Infantry model with this special rule are improved by the current rank bonus of its unit, or in the case of characters, the current rank bonus of any unit they have joined.

In addition, if a unit with this special rule makes a Charge move of 6" or more following a Charge or Pursuit roll that includes one or more natural 6s, all models in the unit gain Impact Hits (1) and treat low linear obstacles as open ground during the turn in which they charge.

Note: This means that models separated only by a low linear obstacle are considered to be in base contact with one another for the purposes of combat and the enemy unit receives no benefits for defending a low linear obstacle against this unit..
If the majority of the models in a unit have this special rule, it may re-roll its Charge roll.
Enemy units engaged in combat with one or more models with this rule have the Strikes Last special rule and a -1 modifier to their Weapon Skill characteristic, to a minimum of 1.
A hand weapon carried by a model with this special rule has an Armour Piercing characteristic of -1.

Note that this special rule only applies to a single, non-magical hand weapon, and does not apply to a model's mount (should it have one). If the model is using an Ogre Kingdoms Ironfist as a weapon (or any other sort of weapon), this special rule ceases to apply.

body: Impact Hits caused by this model (but not its mount) have an Armour Piercing characteristic of -1.

This character replaces the Impact Hits (2) special rule with the Impact Hits (D3+1) special rule. In addition, during the Command sub-phase of their turn, if they are not engaged in combat, a character with a Butcher’s Cauldron may attempt to make an offering to the Great Maw by making a Leadership test (using their own unmodified Leadership). If this test is passed, until your next Start of Turn sub-phase this character and any unit they have joined gains the Regeneration (5+) special rule. However, if this test is failed, a single friendly model within 3" of the bearer immediately loses a single Wound.

A Hunter that joins a unit of Sabretusks gains the Swiftstride special rule for as long as they remain with the unit. For as long as the Hunter remains with the unit, the Sabretusks lose the Impetuous special rule. Note: When a Hunter joins a unit of Sabretusks the unit may adopt or stay in a Skirmish formation, despite the difference in their unit types. Additionally, while joined to a unit of Sabretusks, and one or more Sabretooth remains, The Hunter cannot be targeted by enemy shooting and he can make a "Look Out, Sir!" roll.

Instead of discarding one of their randomly generated spells for a Signature Spell, a model with this special rule may discard one of their spells to learn Fireball instead. This rule may not be used to learn Fireball a second time if it was already randomly generated by this model.. In addition, a model with this special rule has a 4+ Ward save against any wounds suffered that were caused by an attack that has the Flaming Attacks special rule.

A character that can be mounted may choose a mount from the following list. Most mounts are covered in detail on the following pages. Those that are not have their own dedicated entries later in this army list.
A Tyrant, Bruiser or Hunter may be mounted on a:
Stonehorn +195 points • Thundertusk +185 points
Any enemy model that ends its movement within 6 inches of one or more models with this special rule (that are not fleeing or engaged in combat with another unit) must make a Dangerous Terrain Test.
A unit of Gnoblar Trappers within the Command Range of a Hunter who is not fleeing may use the Hunter’s Leadership characteristic instead of their own.

Impact Hits caused by a model with this special rule have the Armour Bane (1) special rule and an Armour Piercing characteristic of -1. In addition, if a unit with this special rule makes a Charge move of 6" or more following a Charge roll that includes one or more natural 6s, all models in the unit gain Impact Hits (1) and treat low linear obstacles as open ground during the turn in which they charge.

Note: This means that models separated only by a low linear obstacle are considered to be in base contact with one another for the purposes of combat and the enemy unit receives no benefits for defending a low linear obstacle against this unit..
1 Kaboom! Constantly mistreated by the Ogres, the cannon explodes spectacularly. The model is destroyed and immediately removed from play.
2 Krrack! With a tremendous crack, the cannon splits along its length, rendering it
useless. The model cannot shoot with this weapon for the remainder of the game.
3-4 Ack! Through its own ineptitude, the Gnoblar Scrapper has become stuck in the mechanism. The model does not shoot this turn and cannot shoot with this weapon during the next round.
5-6 Durr! The cannon may not shoot this turn.
Notes: This weapon shoots like a stone thrower, using the ‘Bombardment’ special rule, a 5" blast template and the Scraplauncher Misfire table.

If a natural 6 is rolled when making a roll To Wound with this weapon, Enemy models whose troop type is regular infantry, heavy infantry, light cavalry, heavy cavalry or war beasts are not permitted an armour or Regeneration save (Ward saves can be attempted as normal).
This model is less vulnerable to the Multiple Wounds (X) special rule. If it suffers an unsaved wound from an attack with this special rule, reduce the number of Wounds lost by 1, to a minimum of 1.

Character Mount: A Stonehorn may also be included in your army as a character’s mount. If so, its points are added to that of its rider. When doing so, the character replaces the Ogre Beast Rider, and the Stonehorn uses the following profile and points value with the same equipment, options and special rules as above:
Sphere of 6-24” 3(6) -1(-2) Bombardment, Cumbersome, Multiple Frost-wreathed Ice Wounds (D3)

Notes: This weapon shoots like a stone thrower, using the ‘Bombardment’ special rule and a 3" blast template. If a misfire result is rolled this model suffers a wound and this weapon cannot shoot this turn. The Multiple Wounds (D3) special rule applies only to a single model whose base lies underneath the central hole of the blast template.
This model ignores the To Hit modifier for Moving and Shooting.

Notes: The Ironfist has two profiles. You must choose which the wielder will use at the start of each round of combat. An Ironfist is a type of shield. A model that is equipped with an Ironfist can use either profile, while maintaining the benefits that a shield provides. Furthermore, whilst engaged in close combat, a model that is equipped with and chooses to use an Ironfist as a weapon improves its armor value (but not the value of its mount’s save, if any) by an additional 1, to a maximum of 3+
Notes: Ranged attacks made with this weapon apply Killing Blows in the same manner as melee attacks.

beastkiller.body:
0-1 per army. Hunter only. Unless wielding a magic weapon, a model with this Big Name (but not its mount) gains the Monster Slayer special rule.

Note: Monster Slayer does not apply to shooting attacks.

mawseeker.body: Models whose troop type is ‘infantry’ only. 0-1 per army. This model (including their mount if it has one) has a +1 modifier to their Toughness characteristic. However, this model is also subject to the Stupidity special rule.

wallcrusher.body: A model with this Big Name (but not their mount) gains Impact Hits (1). In addition, Wallcrushers and any unit they have joined treat low linear obstacles as open ground. Note: This means that models separated only by a low linear obstacle are considered to be in base contact with one another for the purposes of combat and the enemy unit receives no benefits for defending a low linear obstacle against this unit.

mountaineater.body: Models whose troop type is ‘infantry’ only. 0-1 per army. This model cannot be wounded by a roll To Wound of 2, regardless of the Strength of the attack.

giantbreaker.body: This model (but not their mount) has a +1 modifier to their Strength characteristic. However, this model cannot refuse a challenge and neither they, nor any unit they have joined, can Flee as a charge reaction.

kineater.body: Characters only. Unless this character is fleeing, friendly models within this character’s Command range may re-roll any failed Panic or Rally test.

longstrider.body: Models whose troop type is ‘infantry’ only. This model has a +1 modifier to their Movement characteristic.

deathcheater.body: Once per game, you may make your opponent re-roll a single roll To Wound made against this model.

thundermace.body:
| R S | AP | Special Rules Thundermace | Combat S+2 | -2 | Armour Bane (1), Magical Attacks, | | | Requires Two Hands, Strike Last

Notes: Rather than attacking normally, the wielder of the Thundermace may choose to make a special ‘Thunderstrike’ attack. If they do, make a single roll To Hit. If this is successful, place a small (3") blast template so that its central hole is directly over the centre of the hit unit. Any enemy model whose base lies underneath the template risks being hit by this weapon.

gut-maw.body: May be worn with other armour. The wearer of the Gut Maw improves their armour save by one. In addition, for each unsaved wound the wearer causes during a Challenge, they recover a single lost Wound.

spangleshard.body: The Spangleshard gives its bearer a 4+ Ward save against any wounds suffered. However, if a natural 1 is rolled, the Spangleshard is destroyed and it cannot be used again.

cathayan-jet-pendant.body:
A Cathayan Jet Pendant gives its bearer (and any unit they have joined) a 6+ Ward save against any wounds suffered that were caused by a Magic Missile, a Magical Vortex, or an Assailment spell.

Magic Standards

dragonhide-banner.body: A unit carrying the Dragonhide Banner may re-roll any rolls To Hit of a natural 1. In addition, a unit carrying the Dragonhide Banner has the Flaming Attacks Numbing Chill special rule.

tooth-gnoblar.body: 0-3 per model. Single use. After making a Casting roll for a spell from the Lore of the Great Maw, the bearer may choose to use a Tooth-Gnoblar. If they do so, apply a +1 modifier to the result. A model may only use one Tooth-Gnoblar per Casting roll.

notes: Some models drawn from the Ogre Kingdoms army list may be given a Big Name, chosen from those detailed on this page. Each Big Name gives the model certain benefits in the form of modified characteristics and additional special rules:

Core: 1+ Ogre Bulls, Ironguts, Gnoblar Fighters, Gnoblar Trappers and Sabretusk Packs
Special: Leadbelchers, Yhetees and Gnoblar Scraplaunchers • 0-1 unit of Maneaters per 1,000 points • 0-1 unit of Mournfang Cavalry per 1,000 points • 0-1 Ironblaster per 1,000 points
Rare: 0-1 Thundertusk Riders per 1,000 points • 0-1 Stonehorn Riders per 1,000 points • 0-3 Gorgers and Giants
